A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. All 51 pages in each version support comparison, including material relocated within the appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak, backdoor, SQL-generation, image-classification, and adversarial-training experiments, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including monitor performance, attack success rates, SQL accuracy, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds a weighted KL penalty between current and original model outputs on benign inputs to OAT's previously BCE-only model update. This is a limited revision to the stated training objective; the main obfuscation attacks remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The same harmfulness, backdoor, SQL, image-classification, and orthogonality scenarios remain. Dataset coverage, including UltraChat, XSTest, Circuit Breakers, Bias in Bios, SQL-Create-Context, SQLEval, and CIFAR-10, is unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix B.3 removes quadratic-probe transfer claims and replaces an AE-detector reference with TED. However, neither quadratic nor AE appears in the corresponding Figures 10 and 21 in either version, whose comparator sets are unchanged. The PDFs cannot establish whether comparisons were removed or erroneous prose was corrected.

E3.justification: Reported splits, sample sizes, models, budgets, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The revised SQL-evaluation wording agrees with the procedure already described in v1 Section 5.3 and Appendix C.3. Section 3.5's input-probe clarification does not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The same transfer analyses, adversarial-training trajectories, backdoor-trigger and poisoning sweeps, SQL layer sweep, and orthogonality study remain. Appendix figures and Table 2 are retained evidence, not newly added analyses.

E5.justification: Bootstrapped recall confidence intervals and the Pearson-correlation confidence intervals in Table 2 are unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty procedures, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted data are unchanged. Section 3.6 corrects standard jailbreaks from 'reliably obfuscate' to 'do not reliably obfuscate,' matching existing Figure 4 and Table 1. Appendix B.3 also revises qualitative transfer statements, including AE to TED and removal of quadratic-probe claims.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(10), SAE formulation, and detector mathematics remain unchanged; Equation (4) is relocated. No theoretical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added. Algorithm 1's loss revision changes the training procedure rather than theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: latent-monitor vulnerability, malleable representations, attack transfer, and limits imposed by demanding behaviors such as correct SQL generation. The corrected Section 3.6 takeaway aligns with the already-established central account.

C2.justification: Section 8.1 removes the explicit qualification that aggregating probes across layers is not a robust defense, although the supporting counterexample in Section 6.1 remains. This modestly reduces the qualification of the discussion; most mechanism explanations and limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project code-access URL on the first page and explicitly documents averaging layerwise cosine similarities for mean-difference probe scoring in Appendix A.1. Algorithm 1 also exposes the KL term and its scaling parameter. The URL's availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 adds Che et al. (2024), 'Model manipulation attacks enable more rigorous evaluations of llm capabilities,' with a corresponding reference. Section 5 changes SAE monitoring from an asserted previous use to a possible application. The broader related-work positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Scattered grammar, terminology, and wording corrections improve readability. Appendix A.1 places the existing probe-training equations before the attack-training discussion, and Appendix C.4 gains an explanation linking Table 2 to Figure 15. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 is expanded, Figure 22 receives a fuller caption, and appendix displays reflow. Table 2 now appears with its Appendix C.4 discussion instead of floating into Appendix D. The plots, table structures, and overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Section 3.6's reversed takeaway, adding code-access information, and making probe scoring and the OAT objective more explicit improve clarity and reproducibility. The empirical evidence is unchanged. The gain is limited: Appendix B.3 still contradicts itself about TED transfer, and Section 8.1 loses a useful qualification.
